Make a paywall's design live: build it, wait for the build, and deploy it to every location that
shows the paywall. --build deploys an existing build instead, such as an older one to roll back.

--env test deploys to test only: apps using a test key get the build, and end users keep what they
see. Try it on a device, then deploy the same build with --env production. --env production leaves a
build test has of its own in place. Without --env the build goes to both, and test follows
production again: from then on a deploy to production reaches apps using a test key too, until a
build is deployed to test alone.

Asks first when a location shows the paywall and the deploy reaches production, because end users
see the change on their next visit; --yes skips that. Without a terminal and without --yes, nothing
is built.

Warns, and deploys anyway, when a language of the design has texts without a translation: end users
reading it see the design's own language there.

An arm of a running or paused experiment keeps the build it started with; the result names each one.
'voidhash experiment deploy-arm' moves an arm to another build.

Usage:
  voidhash paywall deploy [paywall] [flags]

Arguments:
  paywall  The paywall's slug, name or id

Flags:
      --build <number>         Deploy this existing build, by number or id, such as an older one to
                               roll back (default: build the current design)
      --env <production|test>  Deploy to this environment only: production (end users) or test (apps
                               using a test key) (default: both)
  -h, --help                   Show help for this command
      --json                   Print the API objects as JSON, for scripts
      --project <project>      Project to act on: its id, slug, organization/slug or name (default:
                               this directory's project, then your default project)
  -q, --quiet                  Print only ids, one per line
      --timeout <seconds>      How many seconds to wait for the build (default: 300)
  -y, --yes                    Make the change without asking for confirmation

Global flags:
  -d, --debug              Print each request and full error detail to standard error
      --no-color           Print without colors (also when NO_COLOR is set)
      --profile <profile>  Use a named config profile: its settings override the base config
                           (default: VOIDHASH_PROFILE)

Examples:
  voidhash paywall deploy pro --env test
  voidhash paywall deploy pro --build 3 --env production --yes
  voidhash paywall deploy pro --build 2 --yes
